name: sonnet-criteria-llama31-8b/27
question: I get migraines about twice a month. Should I take something preventively or just treat each one when it happens?
criteria: impact on quality of life and productivity
side effect burden of daily preventives
efficacy of triptans for acute treatment
risk of progression to chronic migraine
cost and insurance coverage of CGRP inhibitors
plausible_answers: Answer A (Acute Treatment Default): Manage 2 migraines per month with triptans as needed — daily preventive medication adds side effect burden that isn't justified at this frequency, and most patients manage well with acute-only treatment.

Answer B (Start Preventives Early): Begin preventive therapy even at 2/month if your attacks are severely disabling — preventing progression to chronic migraine justifies earlier preventive intervention, and newer CGRP inhibitors have minimal side effects.

Answer C (Lifestyle Plus Acute): Prioritize identifying and eliminating personal triggers (sleep, diet, stress) alongside acute triptans before adding daily medication — many patients reduce frequency below treatment threshold through lifestyle modification alone.
sources:
Source 1 (2022, Mayo Clinic, Rochester MN USA): Preventive therapy is recommended when migraines occur 4 or more days per month, significantly impair quality of life, or when acute medications are overused — options include beta-blockers, topiramate, and CGRP inhibitors.

Source 2 (2023, NEJM, Boston MA USA): CGRP monoclonal antibodies (erenumab, fremanezumab) reduce monthly migraine days by 50% in approximately 40–50% of patients — they are well-tolerated with minimal side effects compared to older preventives.

Source 3 (2023, WebMD, Atlanta GA USA): Many patients with 2 migraines per month manage effectively with acute triptans alone — preventive medication adds daily pill burden and side effects that may not be justified for low-frequency episodic migraine.

Source 4 (2023, Reddit r/migraine, USA): Community is divided — members with 2/month often manage with triptans and lifestyle triggers; those who progressed to chronic migraine regret not starting preventives earlier when frequency was lower.

Source 5 (2022, JAMA Neurology, Chicago IL USA): For patients with 4–14 migraine days/month, preventive combined with acute rescue medication is more cost-effective long-term than acute-only treatment when accounting for lost productivity and quality of life.
